The headline measure is the paired width ratio $r=\text{width(arm)}/\text{width(PPI++)}$ on the same draws, with a 95\% interval over repetitions; PPI++ is the package's unless said otherwise. Since width scales as $n^{-1/2}$, $1-r^2$ is the fraction of labels saved. The rule was fixed before any run: a cell is \emph{no gain} if the interval for $r$ lies in $[0.98,1.02]$, a \emph{gain} if its upper bound is below $0.95$ and the arm is valid, and undecided otherwise. After the first results showed that the package's clip matters (\cref{sec:results}) we also read every ratio against the \emph{strongest valid baseline}: the narrower of the package's and the unclipped PPI++ among those whose coverage is valid in the cell (the narrower of the two if neither is), with the same margins. We report both classifications. An arm is valid in a cell if its coverage is not significantly below nominal (Wilson interval) and not below that of PPI++ beyond Monte Carlo error; an invalid arm's width is reported but not counted as a gain. Replacing the Wilson test by coverage $\ge0.94$ leaves the reference-$n$ classes and the range of $r$ unchanged, changes the baseline in $2$ of the $9$ cells without changing a class, and moves $5$ of the $113$ cells of \cref{fig:regime} (the only new gain is \texttt{gene\_expression} at $n=30$). Headline cells use at least 2000 repetitions and small-$n$ or rare-event cells at least 5000. Sample sizes are log-spaced in $\{30,\dots,10^4\}$ as each pool allows, with a reference $n$ fixed before the runs ($500$, except \texttt{forest}, whose pool allows $N=1000$ unlabeled records, where it is $200$); $N$ is the largest the pool allows under a stated cap, with $N/n\in\{1,4\}$ on three datasets.
